dev_practices_debugging.title: Production Bug Root Cause Analysis
dev_practices_debugging.scenario: A pagination endpoint `/api/items?page=1&limit=10` is missing the 10th item for every page request.
dev_practices_debugging.codeSnippet:
def get_page(items, page, limit):
    # BUG INVESTIGATION:
    start = (page - 1) * limit
    end = start + limit - 1  # Line 4
    return items[start:end]
dev_practices_debugging.taskDescription: Identify why the 10th item is omitted and select the correct fix.

options.text: Python slice `items[start:end]` is exclusive of `end`. Line 4 should be `end = start + limit`.
options.explanation: Correct! Python slicing `[start:end]` excludes the upper bound. Subtracting 1 cuts off the final element.

options.text: Line 3 is wrong: `start` must be `page * limit`.
options.explanation: Incorrect. For page 1, `(1 - 1) * 10 = 0`, which is the correct 0-indexed start.

options.text: Items list must be reversed before slicing.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Reversing the list corrupts sorting order.

databases.title: SQL Query Optimization Diagnostic
databases.scenario: A query filtering by `status` and sorting by `created_at` on an orders table is triggering a sequential table scan across 2M rows.
databases.codeSnippet:
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT id, total_amount, created_at
FROM orders
WHERE status = 'COMPLETED'
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 20;
databases.taskDescription: Which composite index eliminates the full table scan and in-memory sort?

options.text: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status_created ON orders (status, created_at DESC);
options.explanation: Correct! A composite index on `(status, created_at DESC)` allows the database engine to perform an index seek on status and stream pre-ordered rows.

options.text: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_total ON orders (total_amount);
options.explanation: Incorrect. `total_amount` is not part of the WHERE or ORDER BY clauses.

options.text: Convert the `orders` table into an in-memory JSON document.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Unindexed JSON documents still require full scans.

dsa.title: Optimal Data Structure Selection
dsa.scenario: You are processing a live stream of millions of temperature readings and must report the top 5 highest temperatures at any moment in real time.
dsa.taskDescription: What is the optimal data structure to maintain top K elements in O(log k) insertion time?

options.text: Min-Heap of size K (root holds current K-th highest; discard elements smaller than root)
options.explanation: Correct! A Min-Heap of size K provides O(log K) insertion time and O(K) space, keeping the K-th largest at the root.

options.text: Sort the entire stream array from scratch after every incoming temperature reading.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Re-sorting the whole array takes O(N log N) per item, which is computationally prohibitive.

options.text: A standard FIFO Queue.
options.explanation: Incorrect. A FIFO queue tracks insertion order, not numerical maximums.

problem_solving.title: API Idempotency & Concurrency Safeguard
problem_solving.scenario: When a network timeout occurs during payment processing, clients retry requests. Some users are getting double-charged.
problem_solving.taskDescription: How should the backend use the Idempotency-Key header to prevent duplicate charges?

options.text: Store the Idempotency-Key in an atomic cache/database. If key already exists and succeeded, return the cached result immediately without charging again.
options.explanation: Correct! Atomic deduplication on the unique Idempotency-Key prevents duplicate processing.

options.text: Ignore the header and charge the credit card whenever a request arrives.
options.explanation: Incorrect. This causes duplicate charges on network retries.

options.text: Ask the user never to click pay more than once.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Network timeouts trigger automated browser or gateway retries outside user control.
